candidate_targets: fusion with negative thoughts about emotions
fight-or-flight activation in response to emotions
contraindications: May be less effective for individuals with severe emotional dysregulation who require stabilization before cognitive defusion techniques.
original_extraction.evidence_text:
Now you can see how the struggle switch got there. Our thinking self created it by telling us that
uncomfortable feelings are ‘bad’ or “dangerous”, that we can’t cope with them, that we are defective
or damaged for having them, that they will take over or overwhelm us, that they are ruining our life
or that they will hurt us in some way. If we fuse with these stories, the switch goes ON and we
perceive uncomfortable emotions as a threat. And how does our brain respond to a threat? It
activates the fight-or-flight response, which then gives rise to a whole new set of unpleasant
feelings!

---

To draw an analogy, suppose a distant relative shows up on your doorstep. You’ve never met this
relative before, but you’ve been told a lot of stories about her. You’ve been told that she’s bad, that
she’s dangerous, that no one can stand her, that the only relationships she has are with defective or
damaged people, and that she always ends up hurting or damaging those people or taking control of
them and ruining their lives.

---

If you truly believed those stories, what would your attitude be toward this relative? Would you
want her in your house? Would you want her anywhere near you?

---

Of course not. You’d do anything you could to get rid of her as fast as possible. But what if all
those stories were false or exaggerated? What if this relative were actually an okay person who had
just been the victim of malicious gossip?

---

The only way you’d ever find out would be to spend some time with her, put aside all the gossip
and slander, and check her out for yourself. You’ve probably already experienced something like
this in your own life. Perhaps there was once someone at school or at work whom you’d heard a lot
of bad things about. Then you spent some time with them and discovered they were nowhere near
as bad as their reputation.
generation_rules: Use analogies to externalize and depersonalize internal experiences
Encourage experiential checking of beliefs rather than accepting stories at face value
pause_rules: Pause after posing reflective questions to allow for internal processing and consideration.
original_extraction.psychological_function: Challenges fusion with negative stories about emotions, promoting experiential contact with feelings without judgment or avoidance.
repetition_rules: Reinforce the concept that stories about emotions may be exaggerated or false by revisiting the analogy and examples.
original_extraction.therapeutic_function: Helps individuals recognize and defuse from unhelpful thoughts that label uncomfortable feelings as dangerous or harmful, reducing the activation of the fight-or-flight response and associated distress.
voice_rules: Pose reflective questions to engage curiosity and self-exploration
